verifiedStrengths: all 25 CB-00 adversarial fixtures have explicit executable proof references
all 30 invariants retain conservative PARTIAL_GREEN status rather than being promoted by fixture closure
live PostgreSQL conformance exists for durable command identity, committed-result persistence, aggregate-version conflict and rollback of partial canonical publication
canonical event, aggregate version and command result can be committed in one PostgreSQL transaction through PostgresDomainCommitter
canon/traceability checks bind invariant rule text, priority and status

releaseBlockers.finding: Durable PostgreSQL enforcement is not universally wired through domain write paths. SW0-12D explicitly excludes universal domain wiring, so the in-memory allocation, fulfillment, remedy and other ledgers can still be used outside the transactional durability boundary.
releaseBlockers.required: Route every consequential first-vertical-slice write through one transactional command/domain boundary or make bypass structurally impossible, then prove concurrent and crash recovery behavior against PostgreSQL.

releaseBlockers.finding: PostgresDurableCommandStore ownership is keyed by a caller-supplied owner token without a per-claim fencing generation. A same-owner concurrent claimant can receive CLAIMED, and an expired long-running owner is not fenced by a monotonic generation at domain commit.
releaseBlockers.required: Introduce a unique claim/fence token or monotonic generation per acquisition/takeover and require the current fence for every canonical/domain commit; add live PostgreSQL same-owner concurrency and lease-expiry takeover tests.

releaseBlockers.finding: The current cumulative traceability matrix still identifies slice SW0-11 and its INV-027/INV-028 proof entries omit SW0-12C/SW0-12D PostgreSQL evidence. The checker validates status/rule synchronization but does not require the cumulative matrix to include the newest release evidence.
releaseBlockers.required: Regenerate the cumulative matrix through SW0-RC1 and strengthen traceability validation so release evidence cannot remain only in supplemental files while the canonical matrix is stale.

releaseBlockers.finding: Title and risk transfer remain intentionally unresolved. The invariant itself requires possession, custody, title, risk, acceptance, settlement and discharge to remain orthogonal, while current proof explicitly states title/risk are pending.
releaseBlockers.required: Keep OPEN-011 externalized; before production transactions, define governed transaction-specific title/risk policy and executable proof without inventing a universal delivered_at rule.

releaseBlockers.finding: Physical lineage remains a bounded proof rather than a durable general split/merge/process model; multi-input/per-lot quantity semantics are not a complete durable ancestry model.
releaseBlockers.required: Model explicit per-input and per-output lot quantities and persist lineage durably before claiming full provenance conformance.

decision: The bounded kernel may proceed to the next hardening release, but SW0 is not authorized as a production-complete release candidate and no invariant is promoted to full GREEN. Close RC1-B01 through RC1-B03 before a second release-candidate GO/NO-GO; RC1-B04 must remain a governed legal/contract policy gate for production transactions; RC1-B05 must close before full lineage conformance is claimed.
next: SW0-RC1A — transactional boundary and fencing closure, followed by refreshed cumulative traceability and RC1 re-review.
